headers.description: Optional headers to send with the request as a dictionary of header values.

Content-Type.description: The media type of the resource being requested, typically 'application/json'.

Authorization.description: The credentials to authenticate a user agent with a server, typically formatted as 'Bearer {token}'.

timeout.description: The maximum amount of time to wait for a response from the server, in seconds. A longer timeout may be necessary for slower network connections or overloaded servers. This is a float type value.

params.description: URL parameters to append to the URL. Sent as a dictionary of key-value pairs.

query.description: The query parameter for search or filtering.

page.description: The page number parameter for pagination. Used to retrieve a specific page of results.

auth.description: HTTP authentication credentials formatted as a (username, password) tuple.

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem), if required for the request.

cookies.description: Cookies to send with the request as a dictionary of cookie names and values.

sessionid.description: Session identifier cookie, used to recognize client sessions on the server.

csrftoken.description: CSRF protection token cookie, used to prevent cross-site request forgery attacks.

proxies.description: Proxy settings as a dictionary, mapping protocol or protocol and hostname to the URL of the proxy.

http.description: Proxy URL to use for HTTP requests, including the port number.

https.description: Proxy URL to use for HTTPS requests, including the port number.

stream.description: Whether to stream the download of the response. If False, the response content will be immediately downloaded. Streaming is useful for handling large files or responses.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not. Set to False to skip certificate verification, which is not recommended unless you are sure of the server's identity.

message.content:
Below is a quick‑start guide to a few popular public APIs that accept an IPv4/IPv6 address and return “company”‑level data (organization name, domain, contact email, phone, etc.) when it can be inferred. All of them expose a simple REST endpoint that you can call with `GET` and receive JSON back. | Service | Endpoint | Key Features | Pricing / Limits | Example Call | |---------|----------|--------------|------------------|--------------| | **ipinfo.io** | `https://ipinfo.io//json?token=` | • Organization name (`org`)
• Domain (`hostname`)
• Company email & phone via optional “company” lookup (requires paid plan) | Free tier: 50k req/month, paid plans start at $5/mo (200k req). | `curl -s https://ipinfo.io/8.8.8.8/json?token=YOUR_TOKEN` | | **ipstack.com** | `https://api.ipstack.com/?access_key=&format=1&fields=ip,hostname,location,organization,company` | • Organization + company name
• Contact email & phone (paid) | Free tier: 10k req/month, paid starts at $9.99/mo (500k req). | `curl -s https://api.ipstack.com/8.8.8.8?access_key=YOUR_KEY&format=1` | | **ipapi.co** | `https://ipapi.co//json/?key=` | • Organization (`org`)
• Domain (`hostname`)
• Company email & phone (paid) | Free tier: 30k req/day, paid starts at $9.99/mo (500k req). | `curl -s https://ipapi.co/8.8.8.8/json/?key=YOUR_KEY` | | **ipgeolocation.io** | `https://api.ipgeolocation.io/ipgeo?apiKey=&ip=` | • Organization (`isp`)
• Domain (`domain`)
• Company email & phone (paid) | Free tier: 1k req/day, paid starts at $19/mo (100k req). | `curl -s https://api.ipgeolocation.io/ipgeo?apiKey=YOUR_KEY&ip=8.8.8.8` | | **ipdata.co** | `https://api.ipdata.co/?api-key=` | • Organization (`org`)
• Domain (`hostname`)
• Company email & phone (paid) | Free tier: 1k req/day, paid starts at $9/mo (100k req). | `curl -s https://api.ipdata.co/8.8.8.8?api-key=YOUR_KEY` | --- ## How to Use One of These APIs (Example: ipinfo.io) ```bash # 1️⃣ Get your free API token # Sign up at https://ipinfo.io/signup and copy the token. TOKEN="YOUR_TOKEN" # 2️⃣ Make a request IP="8.8.8.8" RESPONSE=$(curl -s "https://ipinfo.io/${IP}/json?token=${TOKEN}") # 3️⃣ Parse the JSON (using jq for illustration) echo "$RESPONSE" | jq '.' ``` Typical JSON output: ```json { "ip": "8.8.8.8", "hostname": "dns.google", "city": "Mountain View", "region": "California", "country": "US", "loc": "37.3860,-122.0840", "org": "AS15169 Google LLC", "postal": "94035", "timezone": "America/Los_Angeles", "readme": "https://ipinfo.io/missingauth" } ``` If you upgrade to a paid plan, you’ll also get: ```json { "company": { "name": "Google LLC", "email": "support@google.com", "phone": "+1-650-253-0000" } } ``` --- ## Things to Keep in Mind | Topic | Notes | |-------|-------| | **Accuracy** | Most services rely on BGP routing tables and WHOIS databases. Accuracy varies; some IPs belong to ISPs rather than a single company. | | **Privacy** | Some jurisdictions restrict publishing contact info for private individuals. Paid plans usually filter out personal data. | | **Rate Limits** | Exceeding limits triggers throttling or temporary bans. Use caching or a higher tier if you need high volume. | | **Caching** | IP geolocation data rarely changes. Cache responses for at least 24–48 h to stay within quotas. | | **Legal** | Always check the provider’s Terms of Service before using the data in a commercial product. | --- ## Quick Comparison Table (Paid Plans) | Provider | Starting Price | Monthly Requests | Extra Features | |----------|----------------|------------------|----------------| | ipinfo.io | $5 | 200k | Company email/phone, bulk lookup | | ipstack.com | $9.99 | 500k | Company email/phone, reverse DNS | | ipapi.co | $9.99 | 500k | Company email/phone, ASN data | | ipgeolocation.io | $19 | 100k | Company email/phone, threat intel | | ipdata.co | $9 | 100k | Company email/phone, risk score | --- ### Bottom Line If you just need the organization name and maybe the domain, the free tiers of **ipinfo.io**, **ipstack.com**, or **ipapi.co** will suffice. For richer company data (contact email, phone, risk score), you’ll need to upgrade to a paid plan—most providers offer a small “starter” tier that gives you 200k–500k requests per month for under $10. Pick one that fits your budget and the level of detail you need, sign up for an API key, and you’re ready to start enriching IP addresses with company metadata!
